title: A few things I wish someone told me before I built trading agents
author: NoRecognition3349
selftext:
I've been hobby trading for about 10 years and spent the last 14 months trying to automate it properly. I've built and binned more agents than I've kept running.

For ages, I assumed a larger portion of the problem was me but after reading hundreds of posts on here, X, forums, etc, describing similar failures, the problem often isn't the person themselves. Here is what I actually think is wrong. It's a short version of a thesis which I have built a product around.

1. **Your trading agent (or any agent) is only as good as its worst piece (skill), not its best one.** My risk layer was genuinely good. Position sizing, session drawdown caps, etc, was strong. Didn't matter though. The thing feeding it signals was scraping headlines, truncating posts, and calling it research. Great risk engine sitting on top of bad.. no... terrible intel.
2. **Most of my "edge doesn't exist" postmortems were component failures.** This took a while to see actually. I'd let the strategy run, it would bleed, and then think the "edge" might be imaginary or not automate-able. Sometime's that is true, sure, but in a lot of cases where I knew I had an edge (I trade it manually all the time), it was something upstream that was broken. For instance, I had an agent that was pulling on-chain data but it was polling every 15 minutes instead of 5 and it was also pulling funding rate data from an endpoint that was rounding. Like, its difficult or even impossible to tell those two failures apart from the p&l so i'd kill the automation.
3. **A trading agent is often 6 or many more "specialists" in a wrapper.** Example: You might have a signal generation, research and intel, on-chain analysis, execution, and routing + position + risk sizing and post session review. That's ALOT of moving parts. Each of those is often a full job that people do professionally for years. Chances are you might be good at 2 of these, okay and 1 or 2, and shite at the rest so what makes you think you can guide an agent that WILL hallucinate to build those pieces you don't understand yourself? Be honest with yourself about which is which. Mine was risk, your's might be execution, or volume reading, or whatever else.

https://reddit.com/link/1v3ddt6/video/zh77xhswnreh1/player

1. **The easy fix is NOT learning the other skills.** I spent a stupid amount of time trying to become more adequate at on-chain analysis. I got adequate but adequate is worthless when someone doing that one thing full time is going to see things I structurally cannot. The correct more is to get that piece from someone who's actually REALLY good at that one piece... which runs straight into the next problem.
2.  **Not many will share the piece you're missing.** Someone out these has solved EXACTLY the thing you are stuck on but they ain't going to tell you how. Not because they're precious about it but because the moment they explain how their volume read work's, if its a true edge, it's now worthless. It stops working. This is why the "open source" model that works everywhere else is software doesn't work here in this environment/sector. The value is often truly derived from nobody else being able to see it.
3. **You are almost certainly sitting on something valuable.** That piece or multiple pieces you're good at which you built because you genuinely understand it has value to the person who's spent 3 months failing to build that piece. You just can't "sell" it for the reason I made in point 5. That is, once you tell someone how it works, it is no longer valuable. The edge is missing or they build it since you gave them the cheat code.
4. **You are NOT bad at this. The tools assume you are a whole trading desk.** All of these agents are designed around a team of specialists, not a single agent. There's a quant, a data agent, an execution agent, a risk agent, and so on. You are trying to do all the jobs either on your own, and you don't understand it enough, or using a single agent who isn't a specialist but a generalist.

The gap between "my agent runs" lol and "my agent makes money" isn't just a skill gap, its a structural gap.

So, seven months ago I stopped automating my strategies and started building **Khorr.**

Khorr lets an agent hire another agent for one specific job, for instance, a constant feed of the onchain intel your strategy depends on or a risk review agent after every session or an execution layer if thats your weak point. The point being, the agent that is hired is a specialist at that thing. It does that thing and does it REALLY well.

The part that makes it work is the hired agent does the job without revealing how it does it so you get the output, not the method therefore, the edge/strategy/IP stays with whoever built it. Also, who hired whom, and for what, stays between the two agents.

The closest thing I can compare it to is imagine a private phone call with someone on a desk you don't work it who has a specific edge which gives that desk over 80% win rate.

So the person who's agent is brilliant at volume can finally sell that without giving it away and then rotate the money to buy the onchain intel piece they're bad at from someone else and hey ho, their strategy is now complete and they print millions.

Anyway. It's all in testnet right now. I'm looking for people to run replicas and to bring agents onto it. If that's of any interest to you, DM me. Site goes up in the next few weeks either way.
